senses.definition: With just a quick look.
senses.example: I could tell at a glance which jar held more marbles.

senses.definition: At the smallest amount mentioned, or more.
senses.example: For this project, each robot needs at least two wheels.

senses.definition: At the largest amount mentioned, or less.
senses.example: The bookcase can hold at most three more books on that shelf.

senses.definition: Repeatedly in one direction and then the other.
senses.example: We passed the ball back and forth across the table.

senses.definition: To separate a difficult idea or job into smaller parts that are easier to understand or do.
senses.example: Dad helped me break the report down into three short sections.

senses.definition: To decide you have done enough for the day and stop.
senses.example: We had painted the whole first wall, so we decided to call it a day.

senses.definition: To figure out how something works or what someone means.
senses.example: I began to catch on after I watched the first two turns of the game.

senses.definition: To become popular or start being used by many people.
senses.example: Our made-up hand clap began to catch on at camp.

senses.definition: To reach someone who went ahead or get to the same stage as someone else.
senses.example: I stopped to tie my shoe, then ran to catch up with the group.

senses.definition: To decide something different from what you decided before.
senses.example: You can still change your mind about which story to read.

senses.definition: To find or meet something or someone by chance.
senses.example: You might come across a sketch Dad drew between the pages of that book.

senses.definition: To think of something that solves a problem or adds an idea.
senses.example: We had to come up with a way to carry six cups without spilling them.

senses.definition: To be unable to remember or think of the thing you are looking for.
senses.example: I knew the dog’s name yesterday, but today I draw a blank every time.

senses.definition: To take someone or something to a place and leave them or it there.
senses.example: Could we drop off my library books before soccer?

senses.definition: To fall asleep, often slowly or without meaning to.
senses.example: I started to drop off while my brother read the last page.

senses.definition: To become smaller in number, amount, or strength.
senses.example: The number of birds at the feeder began to drop off when the storm passed.

senses.definition: The height of someone’s eyes when they are looking straight ahead.
senses.example: The museum put the labels near eye level for younger visitors.

senses.definition: To understand something or find the answer by thinking about it.
senses.example: We can figure out which key fits by studying their shapes.

senses.definition: To put missing words or information into an empty space.
senses.example: Fill in your team name at the top of the score sheet.

senses.definition: To do someone’s job while that person is away.
senses.example: Our neighbor can fill in as coach on Saturday.

senses.definition: To learn information you did not know before.
senses.example: Let’s find out where the creek meets the river.

senses.definition: Here is one example of what I mean.
senses.example: We can measure time in different ways. For instance, a sundial uses a shadow.

senses.definition: To make an idea clear to someone else.
senses.example: Could a drawing help you get across why the bridge bends?

senses.definition: To learn how to do something well enough to keep going on your own.
senses.example: It took a few tries to get the hang of the skateboard.

senses.definition: To try something and see what happens.
senses.example: I had never sewn a button on, but I agreed to give it a go.

senses.definition: To look at or talk through something again to understand or check it.
senses.example: Before we played, the referee helped us go over the rules.

senses.definition: To give someone work or a form that they asked you to turn in.
senses.example: Please hand in your drawing before we leave the art room.

senses.definition: To give a reason or idea that makes sense and is worth thinking about.
senses.example: You have a point about the loose strap. Let’s check it before we go.

senses.definition: To stay where you are or wait a short time.
senses.example: Hold on while I find the missing puzzle piece.

senses.definition: To keep a firm grip on something.
senses.example: Hold on to the rail as you walk down the steps.

senses.definition: In just a few words that cover the main idea.
senses.example: In a nutshell, the class voted to plant herbs instead of flowers.

senses.definition: Shared by two or more people or things.
senses.example: The puzzles have something in common. Both hide a triangle.

senses.definition: Over a long time, after the early results have passed.
senses.example: Mending the bag may take a little time, but in the long run it could save us money.

senses.definition: To write something quickly so you can remember it.
senses.example: Jot down the bus number before you close the map.

senses.definition: To notice and remember what happens to someone or something over time, often by making a record.
senses.example: I use a notebook to keep track of the seeds that sprout.

senses.definition: To not include a person, item, or detail.
senses.example: If you leave out the date, we won’t know which page came first.

senses.definition: To think or make plans for what will happen later.
senses.example: We can look ahead and pack a raincoat if the forecast changes.

senses.definition: To remember and think about something that happened earlier.
senses.example: When I look back on that race, I remember the cheering.

senses.definition: To feel happy about something that has yet to happen.
senses.example: I look forward to seeing what color the chicks will be.

senses.definition: To pay attention so you notice someone or something when they appear.
senses.example: Look out for the blue backpack on the luggage belt.

senses.definition: To watch over someone and try to keep them safe.
senses.example: My big cousin says he will look out for me in the crowd.

senses.definition: To check something by reading or looking through it fairly quickly.
senses.example: Can you look over the invitation and make sure it has the right date?

senses.definition: To search for a particular piece of information in a source.
senses.example: I can look up the frog’s name in a guide to pond animals.

senses.definition: To respect someone and see them as a person you might learn from.
senses.example: I look up to my uncle because he listens carefully before giving advice.

senses.definition: To be clear enough to understand or to be reasonable.
senses.example: Drawing the route helped the directions make sense.

senses.definition: To do something that helps balance out a loss, mistake, or problem.
senses.example: We could start earlier tomorrow to make up for the time we lost today.

senses.definition: To fail to understand the main idea or what matters most.
senses.example: If you count every cloud but forget why we watched them, you miss the point.

senses.definition: Almost nothing, especially when talking about an amount or cost.
senses.example: The used picture frame cost next to nothing at the school sale.

senses.definition: Here is a different side or way of thinking about the same problem.
senses.example: The hill is steep. On the other hand, the steep path is shorter.

senses.definition: Again and again.
senses.example: We tried the last line of the song over and over until it sounded right.

senses.definition: To listen, watch, or think carefully about something.
senses.example: Pay attention to which plants grow closest to the water.

senses.definition: To show someone a thing or detail they might have missed.
senses.example: Can you point out where the picture shows the frog’s feet?

senses.definition: To return something to a storage place after using it.
senses.example: We put away the paintbrushes after washing them.

senses.definition: To move something you planned to do to a later time.
senses.example: Rain forced us to put off the picnic for a day.

senses.definition: To notice how separate clues fit and use them to work out what probably happened.
senses.example: When I saw muddy boots and tracks by the door, I put two and two together.

senses.definition: To say the words out loud as you read them.
senses.example: Will you read aloud the last sentence on the page?

senses.definition: As soon as possible or with no delay.
senses.example: The bell rang and we went to the door right away.

senses.definition: To decide that something cannot be the answer or is no longer a choice.
senses.example: I can rule out the square piece because the opening is round.

senses.definition: To use everything you had of something, so none is left.
senses.example: If we run out of paper, we can use the other side of our sketches.

senses.definition: To agree about something.
senses.example: We didn’t see eye to eye about where to build the fort.

senses.definition: To arrive at a place.
senses.example: The team can practice as soon as the other players show up.

senses.definition: Next to one another.
senses.example: We put the two leaves side by side to compare their edges.

senses.definition: To talk louder so people can hear.
senses.example: Please speak up so the class at the back can hear the question.

senses.definition: To say what you think matters, especially when you might feel shy about it.
senses.example: When her partner was left out, Kelly decided to speak up.

senses.definition: One action at a time, in order.
senses.example: Our coach showed us step by step how to serve the ball.

senses.definition: To separate something into its pieces.
senses.example: We can take apart the block tower one floor at a time.

senses.definition: To write down important details you see, hear, or read.
senses.example: We take notes about each bird we spot on our walk.

senses.definition: To let each person do something in order, one at a time.
senses.example: The two teams take turns choosing a question.

senses.definition: To spend time deciding what you think before making a choice.
senses.example: I’ll think it over tonight and tell you which club I want to join.

senses.definition: Through easy times and hard times.
senses.example: The friends worked together through thick and thin until the show opened.

senses.definition: To test something new and see how well it works or how you like it.
senses.example: Can we try out the new track before the race?

senses.definition: To show what you can do in hopes of being chosen for a group or role.
senses.example: I’m going to try out for a part in the school play.

senses.definition: To make the level or strength of something higher.
senses.example: Can you turn up the sound a little?

senses.definition: To appear or be found, often after people stopped expecting it.
senses.example: My other glove may turn up in the lost and found.

senses.definition: To find the answer or decide what to do by thinking through a problem.
senses.example: We need to work out how to share 20 tokens among four players.

senses.definition: To go well or reach a good result.
senses.example: We hope the plan to move the concert indoors will work out.

senses.definition: To do exercise to build strength or fitness.
senses.example: My brother likes to work out before breakfast.

senses.definition: To put words or numbers on paper or in a file so you can use them later.
senses.example: Write down your idea before you forget it.

senses.definition: To give most of your attention to one clue, detail, or goal.
senses.example: The group began to zero in on the broken wheel as the source of the noise.
